findings.confirm: how many Ollama vision OCR requests run longer than OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s) or never return, from the Ollama server log or the paperless-gpt log stopping mid-document
findings.problem: Vision OCR through Ollama runs on a client with no request timeout. OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (PR #1070) is only passed to createVisionLLM (main.go:1461), whose result App.VisionLLM is never read; the OCR provider is built separately in createOllamaClient, which passes no HTTP client when OLLAMA_HEADERS is unset (and a header client without a timeout when it is set). README.md:707 and env_registry.go:99 say the timeout covers OCR.
findings.change: In createOllamaClient, give the client the same timeout: build it with the OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS value (default 300 s, 0 disables) when OLLAMA_HEADERS is unset, and set Timeout on the header client when it is set. Delete createVisionLLM and App.VisionLLM, which nothing uses.
findings.why: A vision model that loops on a page (#875) keeps generating until someone restarts the container, and because OCR runs first in the single background loop (background.go:76-84), auto-tagging stops too.
findings.estimate: about 30k output tokens per 1,000 calls generated by OCR requests that never return (estimate)
findings.assumptions: call mix of 3 OCR pages and 5 suggestion calls per document; 0.5% of Ollama OCR pages loop and generate about 16k tokens before a restart; local Ollama only, so the cost is GPU time and a stalled queue, not money
findings.verify: Add a test like ollama_timeout_test.go for ocr.createOllamaClient against an httptest server that never answers: with OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1 ProcessImage returns an error after about a second instead of blocking.

known.note: open: LLM request hangs indefinitely when the Anthropic API does not respond; asks for LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT. PR #972 (open) adds a timeout only to the /api/generate-suggestions HTTP handler, not to the background loop.

findings.problem: The OpenAI-compatible client (OpenAIHTTPClient, used for suggestions and OCR), and the Anthropic and Mistral clients, are created without a timeout, and the background loop's context has no deadline, so one request that never returns stops all processing.
findings.change: Give every provider client a timeout (one LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT for hosted providers, default a few minutes), or wrap each GenerateContent call in context.WithTimeout.
findings.why: A stalled hosted request blocks the single background loop until the container restarts; the requests behind it are not sent at all.
findings.estimate: no tokens of its own; a stalled queue
findings.verify: Point OPENAI_BASE_URL at a server that accepts and never answers; the document fails after the timeout and the loop moves on.

findings.confirm: how many tokens the tag list takes in a real install (number of tags in paperless-ngx), and cached_tokens on two consecutive tag calls before and after sorting
findings.problem: The tag list in the tag prompt is built by ranging over a Go map (app_llm.go:721), so its order is random and differs for every document. The tag prompt puts that list right after the fixed instructions and before the document (tag_prompt.tmpl:13-15), so the part every document shares is never the same bytes twice.
findings.change: Sort availableTagNames (slices.Sort) at the end of the tag block in prepareSuggestionGenerationContext.
findings.why: Automatic prefix caching (OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible hosts from 1,024 tokens, Gemini implicit caching, vLLM, and Ollama's reuse of the previous request's prompt) can only reuse an identical start. With a random order, every tag call prefills the whole tag list again.
findings.estimate: about 150k prompt tokens per 1,000 calls not served from cache (estimate)
findings.assumptions: tag calls are 125 of 1,000 calls; in half of installs the instructions plus tag list exceed the 1,024-token minimum (about 300 tags) and about 1,200 tokens of it could be reused; documents are processed one after another, well inside the cache lifetime
findings.verify: Process two documents with OpenAI and LOG_LEVEL=debug: the two tag prompts start with the same text up to <title>, and usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens on the second is above 0.

findings.confirm: number of correspondents in a real install and CORRESPONDENT_PROMPT_LIMIT; cached_tokens on two consecutive correspondent calls
findings.problem: The correspondent list is also built from a Go map (app_llm.go:735). With CORRESPONDENT_PROMPT_LIMIT at its default 0 (main.go:832) filterCorrespondentsForPrompt returns it unsorted, so the list after the 560-token instructions (correspondent_prompt.tmpl:33-35) is in a new order for every document.
findings.change: Sort availableCorrespondentNames in prepareSuggestionGenerationContext (the limited path already sorts by score, then name).
findings.why: Same as the tag list: the stable start of every correspondent prompt is reshuffled, so no prefix cache can reuse it.
findings.estimate: about 82k prompt tokens per 1,000 calls not served from cache (estimate)
findings.assumptions: correspondent calls are 125 of 1,000 calls; in 60% of installs the instructions plus list exceed 1,024 tokens and about 1,100 tokens could be reused
findings.verify: As for the tag list: two consecutive correspondent prompts share their start up to <title>, and cached_tokens on the second is above 0.

known.note: open PR: opt-in LLM_METADATA_GROUPING generates the title first, then tags, correspondent, document type and date in one call (5 to 2 calls on their benchmark).

findings.problem: With the defaults, every document is sent to the model five times (title, tags, correspondent, document type, created date; custom fields make six), each time with the whole document and with TOKEN_LIMIT unset, untruncated.
findings.change: Ask for the fields together in one structured call (the open PR #1072), or at least start every template with the document so the five calls share a prefix.
findings.why: The document text is the largest part of each prompt and is prefilled five times per document.
findings.assumptions: 125 documents per 1,000 calls, about 1,300 tokens of content each, three of the five copies saved by grouping
findings.verify: With grouping on, the provider log shows two requests per document instead of five.

known.note: open PR: move the OCR prompt before the image data.

findings.problem: Each OCR request puts the page image before the fixed OCR instructions, so nothing the pages share comes first.
findings.why: The fixed instructions are about 120 tokens, below every hosted provider's minimum, so this matters only for local engines.
findings.estimate: close to zero on hosted providers
findings.verify: On a local llama.cpp or Ollama server, the second page's prompt eval count drops by the instruction length.

findings.confirm: how many suggestion calls fail with a 4xx other than 429 (400 context length or invalid parameter, 401, 404 model not found), from the log line 'all retry attempts failed'
findings.problem: RateLimitedLLM.GenerateContent retries every error three times with backoff, including errors that cannot succeed on a resend: a 400 for a prompt over the context window (TOKEN_LIMIT is unset by default), a 400 for an unsupported parameter, a 401 or a 404 for a retired model. AUTO_TAG_MAX_RETRIES then re-runs the whole document on the next poll, so a permanent error is sent up to 12 times, each time after repeating the calls that had already succeeded.
findings.change: Retry only 429, 5xx and network errors (the OCR path at ocr/llm_provider.go:206 already filters this way); return other errors at once.
findings.why: Each resend of a permanent error pays the full prompt again, and the earlier successful calls of the document are bought again on every poll.
findings.assumptions: 0.5% of documents hit a permanent error on the first call; 3 polls x 4 attempts of about 1,600 prompt tokens
findings.verify: With a mock server returning 400 for every request, one document produces one request per poll instead of four.

findings.confirm: how often OCR answers stop at the limit (Anthropic stop_reason max_tokens, OpenAI finish_reason length, Ollama done_reason length)

known.note: open: LLM OCR stores truncated or empty responses as complete text; proposes OCR_FAIL_ON=truncated,empty.

findings.problem: A page answer that stopped at the output limit is stored as the page text; the stop reason is only logged when the text is empty. On Anthropic with VISION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS unset, langchaingo sends max_tokens 2048, which a dense page can exceed.
findings.change: Read StopReason and treat length/max_tokens as a truncation (#1251's proposal).
findings.why: The cut-off page has to be OCRed again once someone notices, and until then the document's text and every suggestion made from it are incomplete.
findings.assumptions: 2% of OCR pages stop at the limit
findings.verify: A mock provider returning a stop reason of length produces an OCR error, not a stored page.

notes.title: OCR retries miss Gemini and Ollama errors, so one 429 fails the whole document
notes.problem: The OCR retry treats an error as transient only if its text contains 'status code: 429' or 'status code: 5'. That is langchaingo's OpenAI and Anthropic wording. Gemini's error reads 'Error 429, Message: ...' (google.golang.org/genai APIError.Error) and Ollama's reads '503 Service Unavailable: ...' (langchaingo ollamaclient StatusError), so rate limits and overload on those providers are never retried: the page fails, the document fails, and OCR_MAX_RETRIES later OCRs every page again.
notes.change: Classify by status code instead of text: check errors.As for genai.APIError (Code) and the Ollama status error, or extend the match to both formats.
notes.verify: A retry test with errors.New("Error 429, Message: quota, Status: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, Details: []") retries like the existing 'status code: 429' cases in ocr/llm_provider_retry_test.go.

notes.title: VISION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS and VISION_LLM_TEMPERATURE have no effect with googleai
notes.problem: GoogleAIProvider.GenerateContent ignores its opts: the genai config carries only the thinking budget, so the output limit and temperature set for OCR are never sent to Gemini, and the finish reason is not read.
notes.change: Apply llms.CallOptions to genai.GenerateContentConfig (MaxOutputTokens, Temperature) and return the candidate's FinishReason as StopReason.
notes.verify: A test with a fake genai transport sees maxOutputTokens in the request body when VISION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS is set.

notes.title: OcrLimitHit compares prompt plus output tokens with the output limit
notes.problem: limitHit uses GenerationInfo TotalTokens, which langchaingo fills with prompt plus completion tokens for OpenAI and Ollama. The page image alone is often 800 to 1,500 tokens, so a page can be flagged as cut off when its output was short, while Anthropic (no TotalTokens) falls back to a tokenizer estimate.
notes.change: Use the stop reason (length / max_tokens), or CompletionTokens / OutputTokens, instead of TotalTokens.
notes.verify: For an OpenAI page with prompt 1,200 and completion 300 tokens and VISION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS=1024, OcrLimitHit is false.

known.note: #1251 notes OcrLimitHit is only computed when VISION_LLM_MAX_TOKENS is set and is not acted on; the TotalTokens comparison is not mentioned.

notes.title: LLM_MAX_RETRIES=0 still retries three times
notes.problem: NewRateLimitedLLM replaces 0 or a negative MaxRetries with 3, so the documented setting cannot turn retries off for suggestions (for OCR, VISION_LLM_MAX_RETRIES=0 does disable them, per the README).
notes.change: Treat 0 as no retries and keep 3 only as the default when the variable is unset (getRateLimitConfig already defaults to 3).
notes.verify: With LLM_MAX_RETRIES=0 and a failing mock, one request is sent.

notes.title: README examples name a model retired on 2026-11-30 and snapshots shut down on 2027-01-14
notes.problem: The README suggests claude-sonnet-4-5 (lines 253, 263, 674; docs/openai_compatible_providers.md:46), which Anthropic retires on 2026-11-30 (model deprecations page, checked 2026-11-27), and gpt-4o (lines 225, 263, 354, 392), whose snapshots gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and -11-20 shut down on 2027-01-14 (OpenAI deprecations page, checked 2026-11-27). LLM_MODEL has no code default, so only new setups copied from the README are affected.
notes.change: Replace the examples with current models (claude-sonnet-5-5; an active OpenAI model), keeping the note that any vision model works.
notes.verify: A new install from the README example starts and its first suggestion call returns 200.

notes.title: Ad-hoc analysis returns a cut-off answer as complete
notes.problem: analyzeDocumentsHandler calls app.LLM.Call, which returns only the text; the stop reason is lost. On Anthropic, langchaingo sends max_tokens 2048 when none is set, so a table over many documents can stop mid-row and is shown as the result.
notes.change: Call GenerateContent, check Choices' StopReason, and tell the user when the answer was cut off (or pass a larger max tokens).
notes.verify: With a mock returning stop_reason max_tokens, the response carries a truncation flag or error.
